question: Will the Long March 10A lift off before 2027?

calls.reasoning: On 11 Feb 2026 at Wenchang LC-301 a rocket that official Chinese reports (mydrivers, 11 Feb 2026) and Wikipedia call the Long March 10A lifted off under its own power. It flew a suborbital max-Q abort test of Mengzhou and its first stage made a controlled splashdown. The criterion ('completes a liftoff before 2027', fine print: leaves the launch mount under its own power) has no start date, so on its text it is probably already met. The orbital debut (Mengzhou-1) has slipped to early 2027 per China-in-Space (Jul 2026), KeepTrack (Sep 2026) and en-Wikipedia (Q1 2027), so it is only a small chance (~4%) before 31 Dec. The main risk is the resolver counting only liftoffs after the question opened, or not counting the 'Long March 10 system low-altitude demo' as a 10A; I give that reading ~20%. No human market found on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi.

- 11 Feb 2026 (mydrivers/official CASC wording, same day): '长征十号甲液体运载火箭在文昌航天发射场成功完成系统低空演示验证'. The headline says the Long March 10A first stage completed a controlled sea splashdown. The official joint test name was '长征十号运载火箭系统低空演示验证与梦舟载人飞船系统最大动压逃逸飞行试验' (QQ News, 11 Feb 2026).
- en-Wikipedia, Long March 10 page (consulted Nov 2026): lists 11 Feb 2026 03:00 UTC, Wenchang LC-301, as the inaugural Long March 10A test. Single core, 7x YF-100K first stage plus 1x YF-100M second stage. Suborbital Mengzhou max-Q abort; the booster did restarts and a hover, splashing down ~200 m from the recovery ship after ~470 s.
- Nextspaceflight still lists 'Long March 10A Demo Flight' as NET 2026, planned. This tracker may be stale.
- China-in-Space (18 Jul 2026): CMSA's mid-year recap omitted Mengzhou. LC-301 crew access and tower work and the assembly buildings were still being outfitted. Mengzhou-1 likely slips to the first months of 2027.
- KeepTrack (29 Sep 2026): Mengzhou-1 planned late 2026, 'reported slipping to early 2027'.
- en-Wikipedia, Mengzhou 1: 'presently scheduled for 2027'; maiden orbital flight of the CZ-10A. The Long March 10 page says Q1 2027.
- zh-Wikipedia, 梦舟一号: earlier plan was Nov 2026; notes the H2-2026 outlook omitted Mengzhou and that in Jul 2026 it might slip to 2027.
- Oct/Nov 2025 CMSA: Mengzhou-1 on the CZ-10A in 2026 (original plan).
- Status quo for a new orbital CZ-10A launch: no launch scheduled before 31 Dec 2026 as of 11 Nov 2026.
- Resolution instrument: the question text says 'a Long March 10A completes a liftoff before 2027', and the fine print only requires leaving the launch mount under its own power. There is no start date, and no orbital or post-opening requirement is stated. The key ambiguity is whether the resolver counts the Feb 2026 suborbital test (officially named 10A in CASC/press reports) or only events after the question opened.
- Event window: undefined start (text says only 'before 2027') -> 2027-01-01. If the window is taken as question opening -> 1 Jan 2027, about 7 weeks remain as of 11 Nov 2026.
- Searched but not found: any Nov 2026 report of the CZ-10A arriving at Wenchang or a firm Mengzhou-1 date; any prediction market (Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi) on this event.

LC-301 was still unfinished in July 2026 and no launch campaign has been reported, so an orbital launch before 2027 is about 3%. The main residual risk is resolution ambiguity: on 11 Feb 2026 a suborbital vehicle that English Wikipedia labels a 'CZ-10A test stage' lifted off from LC-301 for the Mengzhou abort test. The official Chinese name was a 'Long March 10 system low-altitude demonstration', and the question being asked in November implies the author doesn't count that flight, but a Wikipedia-based resolver might. No human prediction market found.

Chinese media name it CZ-10A and Wikipedia's table lists 'Long March 10A | Test Stage', so a literal reading of 'completes a liftoff' may already resolve YES. But the official test name reportedly used 'Long March 10' and it was a single stage, and a question written in Nov 2026 implies the author may not count it (~40% it counts). (2) The first orbital flight (Mengzhou-1) was officially aimed at 2026, but July 2026 reports had it slipping to early 2027 because pad outfitting wasn't done, and Wikipedia now lists Q1 2027. Mengzhou reached Wenchang around 1 Nov for a rehearsal, so a launch by 31 Dec is about 15%. Combined ~0.49. No human market found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.

calls.reasoning: Two paths to YES. (1) The orbital debut of the Long March 10A with Mengzhou-1 before 31 Dec 2026: Wikipedia says 2027, the pad was unfinished in July, and Andrew Jones reported only 'early stages of preparations' around 1 Nov. Debut rocket plus debut spacecraft with ~50 days left gives ~8%. (2) The 11 Feb 2026 suborbital test left the pad under its own power, but the CMSE, CASC and Xinhua official name is 'Long March 10 system low-altitude demonstration' in prototype form, single stage; only secondary sources call it 10A. A question asked in Nov 2026 implies it does not count. I give ~15% that the resolver counts it. Combined ~0.08 + 0.92*0.15 ≈ 0.21. No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: The main dispute was whether the 11 Feb 2026 test counts as a 'Long March 10A'. Checked the primary sources: CMSE, CASC and Xinhua all name it the 'Long March 10 rocket system low-altitude demonstration' in prototype form (长征十号...初样状态), not 10A. Only mydrivers and Wikipedia tables say 10A. That weakens Run 1's ~80% chance the test counts. Combined with the question being asked in Nov 2026 about the 10A specifically, I put it at ~15%. Second dispute: the chance of an orbital debut in 2026. The search for a November launch date found nothing firm. Andrew Jones' X post (~1 Nov) says only 'early stages of preparations', and Wikipedia's Mengzhou 1 page says 2027. Could not independently re-find the Ars Technica 'early 2027' item. Took ~8%, above Run 2's 3% because preparations have visibly started, below Run 3's 15% because of the 'early stages' wording and the double debut. No market found.
